newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks defy crackdown talk to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks defy crackdown talk to end higher.

text.p: Shenzhen stocks closed up on Thursday due to bargain hunting after morning losses, but analysts warned the markets may be further hit by concerns over possible government measures to curb speculation.

Buying in the afternoon pushed the foreign currency B index up 1.78 points or 1.05 percent on the day to 172.53, after hitting a low of 169.31 earlier in the day. Turnover was HK$184.3 million against Wednesday's HK$130.7 million.
The domestic currency A index gained 15.44 points or 3.09 percent to 515.47 on turnover of 11.4 billion yuan, compared with Wednesday's 12.8 billion.
"Many investors have digested the rumours of a market clampdown and are now jumping back in to buy shares at the lower prices," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
Officials at the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the country's top securities watchdog, declined to comment on the rumours about a crackdown.

Rumours have swirled around the markets for the last two days that China may soon ban several major brokerages from carrying out securities trading on their own accounts as punishment for past trading irregularities.
Brokers said they had heard that at least four brokerages, including Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, China's largest, would be barred from conducting trading for themselves for a period.
"Our own trading license may be stripped for half a year," said a trader at one of the four brokerages rumoured to be facing the penalty.
"Without these big fish, the pool of funds will be much smaller," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Other rumours have suggested that CSRC chairman Zhou Daojiong may step down soon. Officials have declined to comment.
China's stock markets have risen sharply since the start of this year despite Beijing's repeated calls for risk control and caution.
Analysts said A and B share trading is likely to be volatile ahead of the weekend, when clampdown measures are usually announced.
"You may make a lot of money by buying on Friday, but stocks may plunge if measures are announced," the Guotai analyst said.
In the B share market, Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd 2553.SZ ended at HK$5.89 on its first day of trading, compared with an issue price of HK$3.48.
"The price (of Sanonda) is by no means low, taking into account the company's performance," the China Southern analyst said. "I would be careful."
The pesticide maker's B share issue was 10 times over-subscribed last month, according to analysts.
Shenzhen Fangda Industrial Co Ltd was the second best performer in the B share market, soaring HK$0.79 or 6.63 percent to HK$12.70.
